events.title: poíēsis: an exhibition by Tom de Freston
events.summary: The term poíēsis derives from the ancient Greek word ποιεῖν — ‘to make’, ‘to create’ — referring to the act of bringing something into being that did not previously exist. For Tom de Freston, this concept operates simultaneously as artistic method and lived experience: an intuitive, imaginative force that binds grief, love and transformation.

events.title: The Economic Architecture of Cooperation - Professor Axel Ockenfels, University of Cologne, Max Planck Institute for Behavioral Economics, Bonn
events.summary: Abstract Many social and economic problems arise because individual incentives pull against the common good. Drawing on examples from our own and others' research—market failure, organ shortages, and climate change, among others—this lecture examines why cooperation so often breaks down. It then shows how modern economic instruments can design targeted incentive and decision-making structures that foster cooperative behaviour and, in doing so, open up new paths to solving these problems. Biography Axel Ockenfels is Professor of Economics at the University of Cologne and Founding Director of the Adenauer School of Government, as well as a Director at the Max Planck Institute for Behavioral Economics in Bonn. His research is in economic design and behavioural science, and he collaborates with governments and companies on design and behavioural challenges including vaccine procurement, organ and stem cell donation, energy markets, climate policy, and crisis management. He has served on standing and ad hoc advisory bodies for various German institutions including the Federal Chancellery, several federal ministries, and the Federal Chamber of Physicians (Bundesärztekammer). Ockenfels is a member of the Leopoldina and several other German academies of science. Among his distinctions is the Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize of the German Research Foundation. Photograph credit: Fabian Stürtz.

events.title: Welfare Reform and the Imperative of Cooperation - Sir Andrew Dilnot, Nuffield College Oxford
events.summary: Biography Sir Andrew Dilnot is the Non-Executive chair of Oxford University Press. He was the Chair of the Commission on the Funding of Care and Support, which reported in 2011. He was Director of the Institute for Fiscal Studies from 1991 to 2002, Principal of St Hugh’s College, Oxford, from 2002 to 2012, Warden of Nuffield College from 2012 to 2024, and chair of the UK Statistics Authority from 2012 to 2017. He was the founding presenter of BBC Radio 4’s series on the beauty of numbers, ‘More or Less’.

events.title: The Magic of Magnetism - Professor Russell Cowburn, University of Cambridge
events.summary: Biography Russell Cowburn is Professor of Experimental Physics at the Cavendish Laboratory of the University of Cambridge, and a Fellow of Darwin College Cambridge. He has research interests in nanotechnology and its application to magnetism, electronics, optics and healthcare. Before returning to Cambridge in 2010 he held positions at the CNRS Paris, University of Durham and Imperial College London. He is the founder of four start-up companies and the inventor of the anti-counterfeiting technology ‘Laser Surface Authentication’. He has had over 60 patents granted, is a frequent invited speaker at international conferences and was one of the 2015 IEEE Magnetics Society Distinguished Lecturers. He has held two ERC grants. He is a Fellow of the Royal Society.
